questions.question:
Match the following institutes with their respective founders of British India.
InstitutesTheir respective founders
a. Asiatic Society of Bengali. Warren Hastings
b. Sanskrit College of Benarasii. Lord Wellesley
c. Fort William Collegeiii. Jonathan Duncan
d. Calcutta Madrasaiv. Sir William Jones
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

  • Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784 (a-iv).
  • Sanskrit College of Benaras was founded by Jonathan Duncan in 1791 (b-iii).
  • Fort William College was founded by Lord Wellesley in 1800 (c-ii).
  • Calcutta Madrasa was founded by Warren Hastings in 1781 (d-i).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Khurda Uprising of 1817:
1. The Khurda Revolt of 1817, also called the Paika Rebellion, took place in Odisha.
2. It was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu against the British East India Company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

  • Statement 1 is correct: The Khurda Revolt of 1817 is also called the Paika Rebellion and took place in Odisha.
  • Statement 2 is correct: It was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu against the British East India Company.
  • The revolt was sparked by the Company's disruptive changes to land revenue and salt policies.

questions.question: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Benaras.

  • The Hindu College (now Sampurnanand Sanskrit University) was established in Benaras (Varanasi) in 1791.
  • It was founded by Jonathan Duncan, a British officer, and Raja Rameshwar Singh.
  • Raja Ram Mohan Roy established the Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817 (now Presidency University).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): B. R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936.
Reason (R): He later became the first Law Minister of Independent India and the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

  • Assertion (A) is true: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936.
  • Reason (R) is true: He later became the first Law Minister of India and chief architect of the Constitution.
  • However, R describes his later achievements, not why he founded the Labour Party.

questions.question: When was the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1920.

  • The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was formed in Bombay in 1920.
  • It was a broad-based organisation involving communists (S.A. Dange, M.N. Roy), moderates (M. Joshi, V.V. Giri), and nationalists (Lala Lajpat Rai, Jawaharlal Nehru).
  • Lala Lajpat Rai was its first president.

questions.question: Who founded the Theosophical Society in New York in 1875?
questions.option_1: Naoroji Furdunji and Satyendra Nath Bose
questions.option_2: Baba Dayal Das and Madan Lal
questions.option_4: Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madame HP Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott.

  • The Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 by Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott.
  • Its headquarters was shifted to Adyar, Madras (Chennai) in 1882.
  • Annie Besant joined the society in 1889 and came to India in 1893.

questions.question: What gave a major impetus to the cotton textile industry in India after Independence?
questions.option_2: Export of raw cotton to England
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Swadeshi movement.

  • The Swadeshi movement led by Mahatma Gandhi aimed to promote self-sufficiency by boycotting British goods and encouraging Indian-made products.
  • India's first cotton mill, the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company, was established in Mumbai on July 7, 1854.
  • The world's first cotton mill was founded in Birmingham, England in 1741.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Jyotirao Phule:
1. He wrote Gulamgiri in 1873, which criticized the caste system.
2. He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in the same year to promote social equality.
3. Gulamgiri was originally written in Hindi and later translated into Marathi.
4. Jyotirao Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, worked for women's education in Poona.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.

  • Statement 1 is correct: He wrote 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery) in 1873, criticizing the caste system.
  • Statement 2 is correct: He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to promote social equality.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Gulamgiri was written in Marathi (not Hindi).
  • Statement 4 is correct: He and his wife Savitribai Phule opened a girls' school in Poona.

questions.question: In his 'Drain of Wealth' argument, Dadabhai Naoroji stated that India's wealth was being drained to Britain through which of the following means?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • Dadabhai Naoroji identified multiple channels of wealth drain: Home Charges, unpaid exports, salaries of British officials, pensions, interest on debt, and profits of British companies.
  • His book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) detailed this theory.
  • He argued that this drain was the primary cause of Indian poverty.

questions.question: The 'Poona Sarvajanik Sabha' was founded in 1870 by:
questions.option_2: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Krishna Gokhale
questions.option_4: Surendranath Banerjee and Anand Mohan Bose
questions.solution:
The correct answer is M.G. Ranade and G.V. Joshi.

  • The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was founded in 1870 by Mahadev Govind Ranade and G.V. Joshi.
  • It was one of the earliest political associations in India representing educated middle-class elites.
  • It played a key role in the Deccan Riots (1875) and later merged with the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: The 'Madras Native Association' was founded in 1852 by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • The Madras Native Association was founded in 1852 by Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty, P. Ananda Charlu, and V. Sadagopacharlu.
  • It was the first political organization in the Madras Presidency.
  • It primarily represented the interests of merchants and educated Indians.

questions.question: The 'Bombay Association' was founded in 1852 by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • The Bombay Association was founded in 1852 by Dadabhai Naoroji, Jagannath Shankarshet, and Naoroji Furdunji.
  • It represented the interests of merchants and businessmen.
  • It submitted petitions to the British Parliament for Indian reforms.

questions.question: The 'Landholders' Society' (Zamindari Association) was founded in 1838 in Calcutta by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • The Landholders' Society (Zamindari Association) was founded in Calcutta in March 1838.
  • Founding members included Dwarkanath Tagore, Raja Radhakant Deb, Prasanna Kumar Tagore, Rajkalam Sen, and Bhabani Charan Mitra.
  • It was the first political association of modern India representing zamindars (landlords).

questions.question: Who among the following founded the 'British Indian Association' in 1851 in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • The British Indian Association was founded in Calcutta in 1851.
  • Founders included Dwarkanath Tagore, Raja Radhakant Deb, and Debendranath Tagore.
  • It was formed by merging the Landholders' Society and the British India Society.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay. Who presided over it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is W.C. Bonnerjee.

  • The first session of INC (1885) was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee (Wyomesh Chandra Banerjee).
  • There were 72 delegates from across India.
  • A.O. Hume was the founder but not the president.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the historic Lahore session of 1929 where Poorna Swaraj was declared?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

  • The Lahore session of 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • The 'Poorna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed.
  • January 26, 1930, was declared as the first Independence Day.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Sinha (Satyendra Prasanna Sinha).

  • Gandhi returned to India on January 9, 1915.
  • The 1915 session of INC was held in Bombay and presided over by Satyendra Prasanna Sinha (Lord Sinha).
  • He was the first Indian to be appointed as a law member of the Viceroy's Council.

questions.question: The 'All India Muslim League' was founded in 1906 at:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dhaka.

  • The All India Muslim League was founded on December 30, 1906 at Dhaka (now in Bangladesh).
  • Founders: Nawab Khwaja Salimullah, Aga Khan III, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and others.
  • Its first honorary president was Aga Khan III.
  • Its first session was held in Karachi in 1907.

questions.question: The 'Lucknow Pact' (1916) was significant because:
questions.option_1: It united the Moderates and Extremists of Congress
questions.option_2: It created unity between Congress and Muslim League
questions.option_3: It accepted separate electorates for Muslims
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • The Lucknow Pact (1916) was signed between Congress and Muslim League.
  • It reunited the Moderates and Extremists of Congress.
  • It accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
  • It also demanded Dominion status for India.

questions.question: The 'Khilafat Movement' (1919-1924) was led by which of the following leaders?
questions.option_2: Ali brothers (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All of the above.

  • The Khilafat Movement was led by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, the Ali brothers (Shaukat Ali and Muhammad Ali), Maulana Azad, Ajmal Khan, and Hasrat Mohani.
  • It aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
  • Gandhi supported the movement and merged it with the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.question: The 'Jallianwala Bagh Massacre' took place on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is April 13, 1919.

  • The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on April 13, 1919 (Baisakhi day).
  • General Dyer ordered firing on a peaceful crowd in Amritsar.
  • Hundreds (officially 379) were killed, though unofficial estimates are much higher.

questions.question: The 'Rowlatt Act' of 1919 allowed the British government to:
questions.option_1: Arrest people without trial for up to 2 years
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arrest people without trial for up to 2 years.

  • The Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed the British government to arrest people without trial for up to 2 years.
  • It was also called the 'Black Act' or 'Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act'.
  • Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha in protest.

questions.question: The 'Hunter Commission' of 1919 was appointed to investigate:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

  • The Hunter Commission (1919) was appointed to investigate the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
  • It was chaired by Lord William Hunter.
  • The commission condemned General Dyer's actions, but no punitive action was taken.
  • Another Hunter Commission (1882) dealt with education.

questions.question: The 'Chauri Chaura' incident (1922) led to:
questions.option_1: Suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhi
questions.option_4: The launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhi.

  • On February 4, 1922, protesters set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur), killing 22 policemen.
  • Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement on February 12, 1922, because the movement turned violent.
  • Gandhi was later arrested and imprisoned for 6 years.

questions.question: The 'Swadeshi Movement' started in 1905 in response to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The Partition of Bengal.

  • The Swadeshi Movement started in August 1905 in response to Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal.
  • It promoted the boycott of foreign goods and the use of Indian products.
  • It was launched from Calcutta Town Hall.
